title: A module over S^{-1}R is its own localization at S
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $S\subseteq R$ a multiplicative subset, $S^{-1}R$ the ring of fractions [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] and $M'$ an $S^{-1}R$-module, regarded as an $R$-module through $R\to S^{-1}R$, $r\mapsto r/1$. Let $S^{-1}M'$ be the localization of the $R$-module $M'$ at $S$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], an $S^{-1}R$-module. Then the map $S^{-1}M'\to M'$, $m/s\mapsto(1/s)\,m$, is well defined and an isomorphism of $S^{-1}R$-modules; its inverse is $m\mapsto m/1$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00O8 (lemma-localize-finite-gl-dim, line 26881), proof: 'Let $M'$ be an $S^{-1}R$-module. Note that $M' = S^{-1}M'$.' (stated there without proof)
